mainEntity.name: What materials are commonly used for drywall framing?

acceptedAnswer.text: The two primary materials used for drywall framing are wood and light-gauge metal (steel) studs. Wood studs, typically 2x4s or 2x6s, are common in residential construction due to their cost-effectiveness and ease of use. Metal studs are frequently chosen for commercial projects or basements because of their fire resistance, resistance to rot and insects, and consistent straightness. The choice often depends on building codes, project budget, and specific performance requirements.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common materials for drywall framing are wood studs and light-gauge metal studs. Wood is popular in residential, while metal is preferred for commercial due to fire resistance and consistency.
